newsitem.title: USA: PdVSA mulls new unit to securitize oil assets.
newsitem.headline: PdVSA mulls new unit to securitize oil assets.

text.p: State-owned Petroleos de Venezula, PdVSA, is considering setting up a new offshore unit to securitize some of its oil receivables in order to finance its $65 billion 10-year expansion program, a company official said Thursday.
"The proposed unit, called PdV Finance, would recapitalize receivables from the sale of crude oil and products," said Manuel Urdaneta Perez-Matos, PdVSA's coordinator of control and finance.
"Instead of producing barrels it would produce dollars," he added.
The proposed unit, if maintained offshore, could enable Venezuela to earn a high credit-rating for its debts, according to bankers at a meeting in New York, addressed by Perez-Matos.
Venezuela's senior sovereign rating currently is Single-B with Standard & Poor's Corp and Ba2 with Moody's Investors Service, well-below investment grade.

However, an offshore financing unit with arms-length title to oil and refined products receivables could receive a rating as high as the top Triple-A, which would sharply reduce the cost of finance and allow the unit the lend to other PdVSA units, according to Perez-Matos.
It is envisioned that the 100 percent owned PdVSA affiliate would own the assets directly rather than through a trust, he added.

The official didn't say how much finance might be raised through the securitization company. PdVSA is authorized to raise an additional $1 billion this year, on top of current debt levels of $3.8 billion, company sources were reported as saying at the end of December.
The company is budged to remit $7.2 billion to the government this year, the sources said.

PdVSA plans to double crude production to 6.1 million barrels per day over the next 10 years. The company has said it plans to cover an estimated 42% of the total cost from its own resources, with rest coming from associations with private companies.
